blogs.title: From LoRA to BOFT: A Plain-English Guide to Smarter Fine-Tuning
blogs.description: Introduces parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) and explains why orthogonal fine-tuning (OFT) was promising yet parameter-heavy. Shows how the new Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT) method keeps the benefits of OFT while slashing parameters, using intuitive analogies and simple examples.

blogs.title: Butterflies in Your Model: How FFT-Inspired Structures Shrink Fine-Tuning Costs
blogs.description: Demystifies the butterfly structure borrowed from the Fast Fourier Transform. Explains how stacking small, sparse rotations can mimic a dense transformation, enabling BOFT to achieve O(d log d) parameters instead of O(d^2). Includes visuals-in-words for how information mixes layer by layer.

blogs.title: Fine-Tuning as Information Flow: A New Way to Think About Orthogonal Updates
blogs.description: Presents the paper’s information transmission viewpoint: building a dense matrix by routing signals across a grid. Shows why choosing the right sparse factors matters, and how butterfly topologies ensure every input can reach every output with minimal trainable edges.

blogs.title: BOFT vs. OFT vs. LoRA: Trade-offs in Parameters, Expressivity, and Stability
blogs.description: Compares three PEFT families in approachable terms. Covers why orthogonality preserves neuron angles and spectral norms, how block-diagonal OFT can be too rigid, and how BOFT smoothly balances expressivity and regularization. Summarizes when each method shines.

blogs.title: A Practical BOFT Playbook: Hyperparameters, Initialization, and Dropout
blogs.description: Offers a hands-on guide to using BOFT: choosing m and b (depth and block size), identity initialization via Cayley transforms, and the new multiplicative Dropout that switches blocks to identities to prevent overfitting. Includes tips for integrating BOFT into existing training pipelines.

blogs.title: Why Orthogonality Helps: Preserving Angles and Spectral Norms for Safer Fine-Tuning
blogs.description: Explains, without heavy math, how orthogonal updates keep pairwise neuron relationships and spectral norms intact. Connects these properties to training stability and generalization. Frames BOFT as learning a structured bilinear similarity under strong regularization.

blogs.title: One Method, Many Domains: BOFT Across Vision, Language, and Diffusion Models
blogs.description: Summarizes the paper’s empirical results in everyday language. Highlights how BOFT adapts large vision transformers, LLMs, and text-to-image diffusion models with fewer parameters and strong performance. Discusses why shared structure may aid cross-domain generalization.

blogs.title: Beyond Butterflies: Future Network Topologies for Efficient Fine-Tuning
blogs.description: Explores the paper’s open questions and limitations: training-time overhead from multiple factors, and whether butterfly is the best topology. Looks ahead to borrowing ideas from computer networking to design even more efficient factorized orthogonal updates.
